  p.run,

  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,

photoobj_with_neighbor_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  COUNT(n.*) AS neighbor_count_total,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN n.type = 0 THEN 1 END) AS neighbor_count_type_0,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN n.type = 1 THEN 1 END) AS neighbor_count_type_1
FROM
  photoobj p
LEFT JOIN
  neighbors n
ON
  n.objid = p.objid
GROUP BY
  p.objid

photoobj_basic_photometry.name: photoobj_basic_photometry
photoobj_basic_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM
  /* Prefer canonical photometry when available; otherwise fall back to star-type cohort.
     The literal used to prefer canonical is lifted out: 'prefer_source' = 'canonical'.
     This SELECT returns one row per photo object (objid). */
  (
    SELECT *
    FROM photoobj_canonical_photometry
  ) AS p
UNION ALL
SELECT
  s.objid,
  s.run,
  s.rerun,
  s.field,
  s.mode,
  s.type,
  s.clean,
  s.flags,
  s.rowc,
  s.colc,
  s.cmodelmag_u,
  s.cmodelmag_g,
  s.cmodelmag_r,
  s.ra,
  s.dec,
  s.u,
  s.g,
  s.r,
  s.i,
  s.z
FROM photoobj_star_type_cohort AS s
WHERE s.objid NOT IN (SELECT objid FROM photoobj_canonical_photometry)

SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  COUNT(s.specobjid) AS has_spectrum_count
FROM
  photoobj p
LEFT JOIN
  specobj s
ON
  s.bestobjid = p.objid
GROUP BY
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec
HAVING
  COUNT(s.specobjid) > 0

photoobj_clean_with_magnitudes.body_sql:

  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.clean
FROM photoobj_basic_photometry p
WHERE
  -- require a non-null, non-zero clean flag
  p.clean IS NOT NULL
  AND p.clean <> 0
  -- require at least one non-null magnitude among u,g,r,i,z
  AND (
    p.u IS NOT NULL
    OR p.g IS NOT NULL
    OR p.r IS NOT NULL
    OR p.i IS NOT NULL
    OR p.z IS NOT NULL
  )

objects_with_spectra_candidates.name: objects_with_spectra_candidates
objects_with_spectra_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  -- true if there exists a specobj row whose bestobjid matches this photoobj.objid
  (CASE WHEN s_by_best.bestobjid IS NOT NULL THEN true ELSE false END) AS has_spec_by_bestobjid,
  -- true if there exists a specobj row whose specobjid appears in galspecline (i.e. membership)
  (CASE WHEN s_in_galspec.specobjid IS NOT NULL THEN true ELSE false END) AS has_spec_by_specobjid_in_galspecline,
  -- any_spec is true if either linkage method yields a match
  (CASE WHEN s_by_best.bestobjid IS NOT NULL OR s_in_galspec.specobjid IS NOT NULL THEN true ELSE false END) AS any_spec
FROM
  -- base set: all photo objects
  photoobj p
  -- left join to any specobj that references this photoobj via bestobjid
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT sb.bestobjid
    FROM specobj sb
    WHERE sb.bestobjid = p.objid
    LIMIT 1
  ) s_by_best ON true
  -- left join to any specobj whose specobjid is present in galspecline
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT s.specobjid
    FROM specobj s
    JOIN galspecline g ON g.specobjid = s.specobjid
    WHERE s.bestobjid = p.objid OR s.specobjid IS NOT NULL
    -- we only need existence of a specobj that is in galspecline; ensure we pick one if exists
    LIMIT 1
  ) s_in_galspec ON true
objects_with_spectra_candidates.description: Denormalized relation indicating which photometric objects have any linked spectral observation either via specobj.bestobjid or via specobj.specobjid membership in galspecline. Exposes both specobj and galspecline linkage fields so callers can apply specific existence logic.

photoobj_with_spec_presence.name: photoobj_with_spec_presence
photoobj_with_spec_presence.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- boolean indicating whether there exists at least one matching spectral observation
  (s.specobjid IS NOT NULL) AS has_spec,
  -- the specobj.specobjid that matched this photoobj, if any (prefer specobj.specobjid match over bestobjid match if both exist)
  CASE
    WHEN s.specobjid IS NOT NULL THEN s.specobjid
    WHEN b.specobjid IS NOT NULL THEN b.specobjid
    ELSE NULL
  END AS matched_specobjid,
  -- the specobj.bestobjid that matched this photoobj, if any
  CASE
    WHEN s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL THEN s.bestobjid
    WHEN b.bestobjid IS NOT NULL THEN b.bestobjid
    ELSE NULL
  END AS matched_bestobjid
FROM
  photoobj AS p
  -- direct match: a specobj row whose specobjid equals this photoobj.objid
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT so.specobjid, so.bestobjid
    FROM specobj AS so
    WHERE so.specobjid = p.objid
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS s ON TRUE
  -- bestobjid match: a specobj row whose bestobjid equals this photoobj.objid, only considered if no direct match found
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT so2.specobjid, so2.bestobjid
    FROM specobj AS so2
    WHERE so2.bestobjid = p.objid
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS b ON s.specobjid IS NULL
photoobj_with_spec_presence.description: Denormalized row-level relation of photometric objects augmented with a boolean indicating whether there exists at least one matching spectral observation; considers matches on specobj.specobjid and specobj.bestobjid.

FROM photoobj po

  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  -- lift literal column name for extinction_r from a depended view; if not present use NULL
  COALESCE(c.extinction_r, NULL) AS extinction_r
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photoobj_canonical_photometry c USING (objid)
photometric_objects_base.description: Base photometric object rows exposing photometry, positions and type metadata (one row per photoobj.objid).

specphoto_denorm.name: specphoto_denorm
specphoto_denorm.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.ra AS spec_ra,
  s.dec AS spec_dec,
  s.z AS z,
  s.zerr AS zerr,
  s.zwarning AS zwarning,
  s.class AS class,
  s.subclass AS subclass,
  s.veldisp AS veldisp,
  s.veldisperr AS veldisperr,
  s.plate::smallint AS plate,
  s.mjd AS mjd,
  s.fiberid::smallint AS fiberid,
  p.objid::bigint AS phot_objid,
  p.run::smallint AS run,
  p.rerun::smallint AS rerun,
  p.field::smallint AS field,
  p.mode::smallint AS photo_mode,
  p.type::integer AS photo_type,
  p.clean::integer AS clean,
  p.ra AS photo_ra,
  p.dec AS photo_dec,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.i AS i,
  p.z AS phot_z,
  p.extinction_r AS extinction_r,
  pt.name AS photo_type_name
FROM
  specobj s
LEFT JOIN
  photoobj p
    ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
LEFT JOIN
  photo_type pt
    ON pt.value = p.type
WHERE
  -- liftable literal: ensure one row per specobj.specobjid (keep all spec rows)
  TRUE
specphoto_denorm.description: Denormalized view joining spectroscopic rows to their matched photometric objects (one row per specobj), bringing both spec and linked photo attributes and photo_type.name for semantic filtering.

photoobj_with_spec_join_33.name: photoobj_with_spec_join_33
photoobj_with_spec_join_33.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric                                      AS specobjid,
  p.objid::bigint                                            AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision                                     AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision                                    AS dec,
  s.z::real                                                  AS z,
  s.class::character varying                                 AS class,
  s.bestobjid::bigint                                        AS bestobjid
FROM
  specobj s
JOIN
  photoobj p
    ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
photoobj_with_spec_join_33.description: Denormalized rows linking photometric detections to their matched spectroscopic observations (one row per specobj.specobjid), combining photo coordinates with spec redshift and class. Useful as a ready cohort for spatial+spectral queries.

photoobj_star_cohort.name: photoobj_star_cohort
photoobj_star_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.type,
  p.clean
FROM photoobj_star_type_cohort p
photoobj_star_cohort.description: Row-level cohort of photometric detections that are classified as stars (photo_type indicates STAR). Keeps raw magnitudes and basic positional and provenance columns for per-object filtering and selection.

photoobj_basic_projection.name: photoobj_basic_projection
photoobj_basic_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- Lifted photometry literals / null filters: keep raw magnitudes as provided
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  -- Standardize type: use provided type but coerce out-of-range/null to NULL
  CASE
    WHEN p.type IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN p.type BETWEEN 0 AND 255 THEN p.type
    ELSE NULL
  END AS type,
  -- Standardize clean flag: interpret non-zero as 1, zero/null as 0
  CASE
    WHEN p.clean IS NULL THEN 0
    WHEN p.clean = 0 THEN 0
    ELSE 1
  END AS clean
FROM
  photoobj_canonical_photometry p
WHERE
  -- Ensure we keep one row per photoobj.objid (grain) and filter out objects lacking essential positions or photometry
  p.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
  -- Require at least one of the five magnitudes to be non-null to allow color computations downstream
  AND (p.u IS NOT NULL OR p.g IS NOT NULL OR p.r IS NOT NULL OR p.i IS NOT NULL OR p.z IS NOT NULL)
photoobj_basic_projection.description: Canonical projection of photoobj with key identification, positional columns, raw PSF/cmodel magnitudes, and standardized clean/type flags. Use to compute colors and apply consistent null filtering.

photo_type_lookup_36.name: photo_type_lookup_36
photo_type_lookup_36.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value,
  pt.name,
  pt.description
FROM
  photo_type pt
photo_type_lookup_36.description: Lookup table mapping photo_type.value to name/description to interpret object type codes (e.g., identify which value corresponds to 'STAR').

photoobj_base.name: photoobj_base
photoobj_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_base.description: Canonical normalized photoobj rows exposing primary identifying columns, astrometry, photometry (ugriz), and basic observational metadata. Nulls are preserved so downstream filters can decide existence checks.

photoobj_color_diffs.name: photoobj_color_diffs
photoobj_color_diffs.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  -- lift literals out: none needed beyond column names
  CASE
    WHEN p.u IS NULL OR p.g IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE p.u - p.g
  END AS computed_u_minus_g,
  CASE
    WHEN p.g IS NULL OR p.r IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE p.g - p.r
  END AS computed_g_minus_r,
  CASE
    WHEN p.r IS NULL OR p.i IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE p.r - p.i
  END AS computed_r_minus_i,
  CASE
    WHEN p.i IS NULL OR p.z IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE p.i - p.z
  END AS computed_i_minus_z
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_color_diffs.description: Per-photoobj computed color differences (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) derived from photoobj photometry. Keeps one row per photoobj and preserves nulls for any missing band.

photoobj_with_neighbors_join.name: photoobj_with_neighbors_join
photoobj_with_neighbors_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  n.neighborobjid AS neighborobjid,
  n.distance AS distance,
  n.type AS type,
  n.neighbortype AS neighbortype,
  n.mode AS mode,
  n.neighbormode AS neighbormode
FROM photoobj p
JOIN neighbors n
  ON p.objid = n.objid
photoobj_with_neighbors_join.description: Denormalized view joining photoobj to its neighbor relationships (one row per photoobj-neighbor pair). Useful for proximity-based selections and deblending checks. Exposes neighbor id, distance and mode/type codes.

photoobj_basic_photometry_40.name: photoobj_basic_photometry_40
photoobj_basic_photometry_40.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.b,
  p.l,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_basic_photometry_40.description: One row per photo detection with canonical photometry and positional columns useful for color and spatial filters. This view exposes raw magnitudes, positions, identifiers, and commonly used metadata without applying question-specific cuts.

neighbors_proximity.name: neighbors_proximity
neighbors_proximity.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM
  neighbors n
neighbors_proximity.description: Neighbor relationships between objects at the raw pair level; one row per neighbor pair. Useful for proximity/coincidence queries and joining to photo detections.
counter_examples: What is the star in photometrically observed binary star system, of which the neighbor's distance is less than 0.05 and has the following constraints in its color bands, u - g < 0.4, g - r < 0.7, r - i > 0.4 and i - z > 0.4

Show me the photometric observed Galaxy of which the color band magnitude g is brighter than 22, and the other constraints as following, u - g >= -0.27 but < 0.71, g - r >= -0.24 but < 0.35, r - i >= -0.27 but < 0.57, and i - z >= -0.35 but < 0.7. Rerank the result with descent order by color band magnitude g

photo_with_close_neighbor.name: photo_with_close_neighbor
photo_with_close_neighbor.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.b,
  p.l,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance
FROM
  photoobj AS p
JOIN
  neighbors AS n
    ON p.objid = n.objid
WHERE
  n.distance <= /*max_distance*/ 30.0
photo_with_close_neighbor.description: Denormalized rows combining photo detections with their neighbor pair info for neighbors within a configurable distance. Keeps one row per photoobj.objid + neighborobjid pair and exposes both photo fields and neighbor.distance for easy downstream filtering and selection.
counter_examples: What is the star in photometrically observed binary star system, of which the neighbor's distance is less than 0.05 and has the following constraints in its color bands, u - g < 0.4, g - r < 0.7, r - i > 0.4 and i - z > 0.4

photo_type_lookup_43.name: photo_type_lookup_43
photo_type_lookup_43.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value,
  pt.name,
  lower(pt.name) AS name_lower
FROM
  photo_type pt
photo_type_lookup_43.description: Lookup of photo_type codes to normalized lowercase names to enable case-insensitive matching of type semantics (e.g., 'galaxy').

photoobj_with_type_44.name: photoobj_with_type_44
photoobj_with_type_44.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.r,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.type,
  t.name AS photo_type_name,
  lower(t.name) AS photo_type_name_lower
FROM
  photoobj_canonical_photometry p
LEFT JOIN
  photo_type t
ON
  p.type = t.value
photoobj_with_type_44.description: Denormalized join of photoobj rows with their photo_type name (lowercased) so queries can filter on type semantics together with photometric columns.

photoobj_with_type_45.name: photoobj_with_type_45
photoobj_with_type_45.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.type,
  pt.name AS photo_type_name,
  pt.description AS photo_type_description,
  p.r,
  p.extinction_r
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photo_type pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_45.description: Denormalized photoobj rows joined to their photo_type name/description. One row per photoobj.objid with both numeric type code and human-readable type fields, enabling convenient filtering by type name without repeating join logic.

photoobj_galaxy_cohort_46.name: photoobj_galaxy_cohort_46
photoobj_galaxy_cohort_46.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.type
FROM
  photoobj AS p
JOIN
  photo_type AS pt
ON
  p.type = pt.value
WHERE
  pt.name = 'GALAXY'
  AND p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
photoobj_galaxy_cohort_46.description: Cohort of photoobj rows that are classified as galaxies (joined via photo_type) and have all five magnitudes present. Exposes raw mags and objid for further filtering and ranking.

photoobj_photometric_catalog.name: photoobj_photometric_catalog
photoobj_photometric_catalog.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.i        AS cmodelmag_i,
  p.z        AS cmodelmag_z,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd,
  p.loadversion
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_photometric_catalog.description: Canonical photometric object records with photometry, positions and basic imaging metadata; preserves one row per photoobj and normalizes column types/nullable semantics for reuse in cohorts and color computations.

photoobj_star_photometry.name: photoobj_star_photometry
photoobj_star_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.type,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode
FROM photoobj_star_type_cohort p
WHERE p.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.type IS NOT NULL
  -- liftable literals for downstream filters: require detection has non-null r-band magnitude
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
photoobj_star_photometry.description: Cohort of photometric detections that correspond to star-like sources (photoobj.type indicating star). Exposes photometry and sky coords to apply color/magnitude filters downstream.

photoobj_neighbor_counts.name: photoobj_neighbor_counts
photoobj_neighbor_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  COUNT(n.neighborobjid) AS neighbor_count,
  MIN(n.distance) AS nearest_neighbor_distance
FROM
  photoobj p
LEFT JOIN
  neighbors n
ON
  n.objid = p.objid
  AND n.neighborobjid IS NOT NULL
  -- liftable literal: only consider neighbors within this maximum distance (arcsec)
  AND n.distance <= 60.0
GROUP BY
  p.objid
photoobj_neighbor_counts.description: Per-photoobj neighbor summary: counts and nearest neighbor distance by neighbor type/mode. Useful for filtering isolated sources or deblending concerns.

photoobj_star_photometry_50.name: photoobj_star_photometry_50
photoobj_star_photometry_50.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags
FROM photoobj AS p
JOIN photoobj_star_type_cohort AS s USING (objid)
-- prefer canonical photometry for extinction and mjd when available
LEFT JOIN photoobj_canonical_photometry AS c USING (objid)
-- lift literals: none used here; selection of stellar sources is via photoobj_star_type_cohort membership
WHERE p.objid = s.objid
-- carry only one row per objid (photoobj.objid is primary key)
photoobj_star_photometry_50.description: Row-level cohort of photometrically observed objects that are classified as stars (photoobj.type codes for stellar sources). Exposes photometry, positions, detection metadata and raw cmodel magnitudes for downstream color/magnitude cuts.

photoobj_with_spec_match.name: photoobj_with_spec_match
photoobj_with_spec_match.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid                                      AS objid,
  p.run                                        AS run,
  p.rerun                                      AS rerun,
  p.field                                      AS field,
  p.ra                                         AS ra,
  p.dec                                        AS dec,
  p.u                                          AS u,
  p.g                                          AS g,
  p.r                                          AS r,
  p.i                                          AS i,
  p.z                                          AS z,
  p.cmodelmag_u                                AS cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g                                AS cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r                                AS cmodelmag_r,
  p.extinction_r                               AS extinction_r,
  p.mjd                                        AS mjd,
  s.bestobjid                                  AS bestobjid,
  s.specobjid                                  AS specobjid,
  s.z                                          AS z,
  s.class                                      AS class,
  s.subclass                                   AS subclass,
  s.zwarning                                   AS zwarning
FROM
  photoobj p
LEFT JOIN
  specobj s
ON
  p.objid = s.bestobjid

semantic_filters.join_type: LEFT JOIN specobj ON photoobj.objid = specobj.bestobjid

photoobj_with_spec_match.description: Denormalized view joining photometric objects to spectroscopic records where available (photoobj.objid -> specobj.bestobjid), exposing spectroscopic redshift and classification alongside photometry for cross-matching and vetting.

photoobj_base_52.name: photoobj_base_52
photoobj_base_52.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.type,
  p.run,
  p.field
FROM photoobj p
WHERE p.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND (p.clean IS NULL OR p.clean <> 0 OR p.type IS NOT NULL)
photoobj_base_52.description: Canonical cleaned projection of the photoobj table exposing identifiers, celestial coordinates, photometric magnitudes, object classification and basic metadata. Normalizes numeric columns as-is and ensures objid is present for row-level operations.

photoobj_photometric_colors.name: photoobj_photometric_colors
photoobj_photometric_colors.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  -- lift color cut literals out of the view: colors computed here; any selection thresholds applied outside
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  p.type
FROM
  photoobj_basic_photometry AS p
photoobj_photometric_colors.description: Row-level cohort projecting photoobj magnitudes and computed common colors (u-g, g-r) to support photometric color-based selection and cuts.

photoobj_with_type_name.name: photoobj_with_type_name
photoobj_with_type_name.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.name AS type_name
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photo_type pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name.description: Denormalized photo objects joined to their photo type name. One row per photoobj with accompanying type name, enabling queries that filter by type name without repeating joins.

specobj_base_projection.name: specobj_base_projection
specobj_base_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric                                 AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint                                  AS bestobjid,
  s.class::text                                        AS class,
  s.z::real                                            AS z
FROM specobj s
specobj_base_projection.description: Canonical projection of spectroscopic objects exposing bestobjid linkage, spectroscopic classification, and redshift for spectroscopic filters and joins to photometry.

photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.name: photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid
photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS object_id,
  p.ra AS right_ascension,
  p.dec AS declination,
  p.g AS g_mag,
  s.class AS spec_class,
  s.z AS spec_z
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.description: Denormalized join of photoobj rows to their best spectroscopic match (specobj) exposing photo object id, coordinates, g magnitude and spectroscopic class and redshift — one row per photoobj that has a matching specobj.

spec_phot_links.name: spec_phot_links
spec_phot_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.g AS g,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.class AS class,
  s.z AS z
FROM photoobj_basic_photometry p
JOIN specobj s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
spec_phot_links.description: Denormalized one-row-per-photometric-object that has an associated spectrum: joins specobj (spectroscopic data) to photoobj (photometry) via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid, exposing both photometry and spectroscopic classification/redshift for easy cohort filters.
